_comment: Birdex typing. Every species gets exactly one GUILD (how it makes a
living) and zero or more TRAITS (how it nests, forages, behaves). Both are
derived from taxonomic family, which birdex.json has for 100% of the
roster - so this table is global: add a European or Australian bird and it
types correctly without touching anything here.
ELEMENTS are different. They are hand-awarded, rare, and each carries its
own note explaining why that particular bird earned it. They are not
derivable and should stay scarce enough to mean something.
label = one or two words, shown on the badge.

raptor.label: Raptor
raptor.flavor: Takes live vertebrate prey on the wing or the ground.

scavenger.label: Scavenger
scavenger.flavor: Finds the dead before anything else does.

piscivore.label: Fisher
piscivore.flavor: Makes its living out of water, on fish and swimming prey.

prober.label: Prober
prober.flavor: Works soft ground and shallows by feel, bill buried.

dabbler.label: Dabbler
dabbler.flavor: Upends and strains vegetation from the water's surface.

insectivore.label: Insectivore
insectivore.flavor: Lives on insects - gleaned, hawked, or hammered out of wood.

granivore.label: Granivore
granivore.flavor: Seeds and grain, cracked in a heavy conical bill.

nectarivore.label: Nectarivore
nectarivore.flavor: Runs on sugar, and burns it faster than any other bird.

frugivore.label: Frugivore
frugivore.flavor: Follows the fruit, wandering wherever the berries are.

omnivore.label: Omnivore
omnivore.flavor: Eats whatever is going. Usually the one thriving near people.

aerialist.label: Aerialist
aerialist.flavor: Feeds in flight - most of its life is spent off the ground.

bark-forager.label: Bark Forager
bark-forager.flavor: Works trunks and limbs for what is hiding under the bark.

cavity-nester.label: Cavity
cavity-nester.flavor: Raises its brood inside a hole, cut or inherited.

ground-nester.label: Ground
ground-nester.flavor: Nests on bare earth. Camouflage instead of walls.

ground-dweller.label: Terrestrial
ground-dweller.flavor: Makes its living on foot, scratching and running rather than flitting.

burrow.label: Burrow
burrow.flavor: Raises its young down a tunnel in the earth - dug, or inherited from something that dug it.

nocturnal.label: Nocturnal
nocturnal.flavor: Hunts by dark, and is built to do it silently.

waterbird.label: Waterbird
waterbird.flavor: Swims. At home on water rather than merely beside it.

shorebird.label: Shorebird
shorebird.flavor: Works the tideline, following the water in and out.

seabird.label: Seabird
seabird.flavor: Coastal and pelagic - salt water is the home range.

colonial.label: Colonial
colonial.flavor: Nests in crowds, and defends the crowd rather than the nest.

cacher.label: Cacher
cacher.flavor: Hides food for later, and remembers where it put it.

mimic.label: Mimic
mimic.flavor: Steals other birds' songs, and sometimes car alarms.

brood-parasite.label: Parasite
brood-parasite.flavor: Lays in other birds' nests and lets them do the work.

ice.label: Ice
ice.flavor: Built for cold that kills other birds.

psychic.label: Psychic
psychic.flavor: Cognition well past what a bird brain should manage.

ghost.label: Ghost
ghost.flavor: Silent, pale, and mostly never seen.

dark.label: Dark
dark.flavor: Clever in ways that unsettle people.

dragon.label: Dragon
dragon.flavor: An old lineage that outlasted the things that should have ended it.

family._icteridae_note: Icteridae is too mixed for a shared trait: marsh blackbirds and grackles nest in colonies, orioles build solitary pouches, meadowlarks hold territories, cowbirds don't nest at all. Colonial is assigned per genus below.

species._audit_comment: Everything below came out of cross-checking each entry's badges against its own description (tools/audit-types.py). Ducks nest on the ground as a family; these five use tree cavities instead.

picoides-arcticus.note: Follows fire. Moves into stands of freshly burned pine within a year of a burn, and largely vanishes once the beetles do.

melanerpes-lewis.note: Breeds in burned pine, and flycatches over the open ground a fire leaves behind.

cinclus-mexicanus.note: Walks into a torrent and keeps walking along the bottom, feeding on the streambed underwater.

pandion-haliaetus.note: Dives feet-first and fully under, with a reversible outer toe for holding fish that fight back.

megaceryle-alcyon.note: Hunts by hurling itself headlong into the water from a perch.

phalaenoptilus-nuttallii.note: The only bird known to truly hibernate - torpid in a rock crevice for weeks, body temperature near freezing.

acanthis-flammea.note: Winters further north than almost anything else, tunnelling into snow to roost.

leucosticte-tephrocotis.note: Nests on alpine talus and feeds on insects blown onto permanent snowfields.

salpinctes-obsoletus.note: Paves a path of flat stones to the entrance of its nest, and nobody is certain why.

catherpes-mexicanus.note: Lives on sheer canyon walls, and sings a falling cascade of notes down them.

nucifraga-columbiana.note: Caches tens of thousands of seeds across miles of ground and relocates them months later from memory.

tyto-alba.note: Flies in near silence on fringed feathers and hunts in complete darkness by hearing alone.

corvus-corax.note: Solves problems it has never seen, holds grudges against individual humans, and appears to enjoy both.

antigone-canadensis.note: One of the oldest bird lineages still flying - effectively unchanged in the fossil record for millions of years.

aquila-chrysaetos.note: Takes prey heavier than itself and has been flown at wolves.
